title: Carebridge POC security QnA — annotated evidence and workshop notes
content:
Executive summary:

This document collects the security Q&A we did with Carebridge during the Feb 9–11 POC workshop, annotated responses to the customer questionnaire, and the reference evidence artifacts we uploaded to the shared evidence bucket. It is intended for internal reviewers (sec, solutions engineering, and sales engineering) and the Carebridge compliance lead. Status: in_review — expect follow-up edits from SE and infra owners before creating a customer-facing pack.

Scope and context:
- Customer: Carebridge (healthcare SaaS, HIPAA scope) conducting a 6-week Dedicated capacity POC with optional VPC peering and CMK integration.
- Focus areas: network isolation, key management, data residency, audit logging, and vulnerability management.
- Deployment model in POC: Redwood Dedicated in us-west-2 with VPC peering (customer-managed transit), option for on-prem connector later.

What changed since initial packet (summary of deltas):
- Added annotated diagram of VPC peering topology (artifact: s3://redwood-evidence/carebridge/topology-2026-02-10.png).
- Clarified KMS integration options: BYOK via AWS KMS key policy vs Redwood-managed CMK (documented in infra PR and Confluence).
- Included recent CVE remediation timeline for the runtime kernels (commit 40b9f2a + release notes excerpt).
- Flagged two open items requiring action from infra and SE: (1) proof-of-rotation demo with customer CMK, (2) clarified log retention SLA for audit logs forwarded to customer CloudWatch account.

Annotated Q&A (customer questionnaire excerpts and our responses):
Q1: How do you isolate customer data from other tenants?
A1: Dedicated capacity is deployed on tenant-isolated GPU pools and VPC peering isolates network traffic. We enforce namespace separation at the orchestration layer; KV cache is scoped per-deployment and never persisted to shared storage. Evidence: isolation-architecture.pdf (S3 link in linked_artifacts). Note: for the POC we used NAT-based egress rules and customer-managed route tables — see topology diagram.

Q2: Key management and encryption at rest?
A2: Data at rest in Dedicated deployments is encrypted using AES-256. Customers can provide an AWS CMK (BYOK) via cross-account grant. We also offer Redwood-managed CMK for faster onboarding; detailed key policy examples are in the Confluence runbook. Evidence: kms-policy-samples.txt and demo script (GitHub commit). Action: infra to produce a step-by-step BYOK run-through for the next workshop (owner: Jasper Liu, due 2026-03-12).

Q3: How are logs and audit trails handled, and can logs be forwarded to customer accounts?
A3: Application and audit logs are written to our observability pipeline and can be forwarded to customer CloudWatch or an S3 bucket via subscription. There is a configurable retention policy; default is 90 days for operational traces and 365 days for audit logs under enterprise add-on. Evidence: log-forwarding-playbook.pdf. Open question: confirm SLA for retention changes during POC (owner: Mariana Silva).

Q4: Vulnerability management and patching cadence?
A4: Kernel and runtime patches follow our monthly cadence with emergency patching for high/critical CVEs. We supplied a recent CVE rollup for the runtime (see linked commit and release-notes excerpt). Evidence: vuln-rollup-2026-02.pdf. Note: customer asked for exported SBOM for components used in the Dedicated runtime — SE to provide.

Q5: Penetration testing and third-party attestations?
A5: Redwood performs annual third-party penetration tests and maintains SOC2 Type II. We can share redacted reports under NDA. Evidence: soc2-redacted-2025.pdf (S3). Action: Sales to request NDA template if Carebridge wants full SOC2 report.

Workshop notes (Feb 9–11):
- Day 1: Intro + architecture review. Customer emphasized HIPAA PHI flow: ingestion -> tokenization -> model inference -> optional downstream HL7 export. We mapped tokenization milestone to the upcoming Optimize feature (cache-by-hash).
- Day 2: Hands-on demo of VPC peering and KMS BYOK flow. Demo succeeded; customer requested a proof-of-rotation script that performs a key rotation without downtime.
- Day 3: Risk discussion and next steps. Customer requested (a) SBOM for runtime, (b) longer retention for audit logs during POC, and (c) a written escalation path for incident response within POC SLA.

Open items and owners (short actionable list):
- BYOK rotation demo script — owner: Jasper Liu — due 2026-03-12.
- Audit log retention confirmation and updated SLA wording — owner: Mariana Silva — due 2026-03-08.
- Export SBOM for Dedicated runtime — owner: Ravi Menon (applied-ml infra) — due 2026-03-15.
- Confirm whether customer wants redacted SOC2 or full under NDA — owner: Noah Patel (solutions engineering) — due 2026-03-07.

Evidence index (what we uploaded to the evidence bucket for easy customer access):
- topology-2026-02-10.png (VPC peering diagram)
- isolation-architecture.pdf (deployment isolation details)
- kms-policy-samples.txt (policy examples and cross-account grant steps)
- log-forwarding-playbook.pdf (how to forward logs to customer account)
- vuln-rollup-2026-02.pdf (CVE list and remediation timeline)
- soc2-redacted-2025.pdf (redacted attestation)

Reviewer notes and suggested edits before customer pack: 
- Infra should add a brief step-by-step screenshot flow for BYOK (console + CLI) — customers liked visuals during the demo.
- Legal/sales: prepare NDA template link for SOC2 exchange if requested.
- Solutions engineering: include a short incident response (IR) runbook tailored to POC scope (who to call, escalation timeframes).

Contacts during POC:
- Customer compliance lead: Dana Morris (danam@carebridge.example)
- Redwood SE lead: Noah Patel (noah.p@redwood.ai)
- Redwood infra lead: Jasper Liu (jasper.l@redwood.ai)
- Redwood security contact (packet reviewer): Eleanor Park (eleanor.p@redwood.ai)

Appendix — quick audit mapping (top-level):
- Network isolation -> evidence: topology-2026-02-10.png, isolation-architecture.pdf
- Key management -> evidence: kms-policy-samples.txt, BYOK-demo-logs.txt
- Logging & audit -> evidence: log-forwarding-playbook.pdf, cloudwatch-forwarder-config.json
- Vulnerability mgmt -> evidence: vuln-rollup-2026-02.pdf, release-notes-2026-02-05.txt

If you are reviewing: please add inline comments in Confluence runbook link and ping me on Slack if you want to schedule a 30-minute dry-run before we share this with Carebridge.

Last edited notes: 2026-03-05 — added vuln rollup and clarified BYOK policy example.
